messages:
Ravi: Heads-up: new onboarding sample for Cloudflare workers fails at startup. getting 'Unexpected token export' from @redwood/sdk and TS in editor shows the client types as `any`.
Aziza: can you paste the exact import and package.json from the sample? sounds like resolution mismatch between runtime and types.
Ravi: import: `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'`. sample package.json has "type": "module" and uses esbuild default. SDK publishes cjs + esm in dist.
Marta: runtime error usually means runtime picked a cjs bundle while the file looks ESM. Check SDK's package.json `exports` map; if it's missing explicit import/require keys, some bundlers pick wrong entry.
Ravi: SDK pkg.json has `main`, `module`, and `types: dist/index.d.ts` but no export map.
Jon: without exports, Node/resolvers choose heuristics. For edge runtimes it's safer to publish an `exports` map with explicit import/require fields + .mjs/.cjs outputs. Also ensure d.ts files are reachable for subpath imports.
Aziza: the `any` types issue likely stems from TS resolving a generated d.ts that's not aligned with the runtime entry (or an overload fallback to `any`). Are there fallback overloads using `any` in the SDK type surface?
Ravi: yes there is a fallback overload `createClient(config: any): any` to keep backwards compat. maybe tsserver prefers that.
Marta: try this quick local hack: in the sample's esbuild config, add `conditions: ['worker', 'import']` and alias `@redwood/sdk` -> `node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/esm`. if that fixes runtime and types, it's a good clue.
Ravi: did that, runtime error went away but editor still shows `createClient` as `any`.
Jon: then TS is probably loading a different d.ts (maybe from root dist/index.d.ts) that contains the `any` fallback. We should emit per-format declaration files or a small forwarding `dist/esm/index.d.ts` that re-exports the root types so TS resolves the same shape as runtime.
Aziza: also rework public API to avoid raw `any` fallbacks. Prefer `unknown` for a catch-all overload, or reorder overloads so generics are matched first. A constrained signature like `createClient<T extends ConfigBase>(cfg: T): ClientFor<T>` helps inference.
Marta: CI idea: add a TS compatibility job that runs `tsc --noEmit` against a set of consumer tsconfigs (module:ESNext + module:CommonJS + moduleResolution:bundler) and fail on changes. That would have caught this earlier.
Ravi: I created a minimal repro: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-repros/edge-ts-179001 (branch `exports-and-types`). includes sample and script to link local sdk build.
CI-Bot: repro build: esbuild succeeded with alias, but tsc-check failed on workspace due to node14 target not understanding .mjs in exports (job 134).
Jon: we'll keep cjs outputs for older node. publish exports map like: `".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs" }` and keep `types: dist/index.d.ts`. Add `dist/esm/index.d.ts` forwarding to help TS.
Aziza: I'll open a PR for the typing cleanup: remove raw `any` fallback, add constrained generic overloads, and include a small index.d.ts per-format. Also add a small `tests/ts-compat/edge.ts` using `tsd` to assert inferred types.
Marta: I'll update the edge sample README with recommended esbuild snippet: 
```js
esbuild.build({
  conditions: ['worker', 'import'],
  alias: { '@redwood/sdk': path.resolve(__dirname, '../node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/esm') }
})
```
Ravi: actions: 1) Aziza PR for types + d.ts shims, 2) Jon add tsc compat job to CI, 3) Marta docs update, 4) Ravi will test publishing with export map on a canary tag.
Aziza: assigning to me for the types work. I'll post links to PRs shortly.
Ravi: thanks all. reopening if anything breaks in canary. :thumbsup:
